mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5pp does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson's r < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO rise > 1% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong demand environment and labor market, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% MoM AND UNRATE falls > 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with an increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% signals a supportive monetary policy and strong supply-side response, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson's r < 0.1).
